gate_name.description: The twelve §8.2 promotion gates; mirrors repair-transaction.schema.json's gate_name.

mutation_campaign.description: Gate 6/7 campaign coverage: mutant-by-mutant detection results (RFC 0032 gate table). A mutant the campaign never ran is evidence of nothing and is counted under `not_run`, never under `detected`.

corpus.description: Identity of the held-out mutant corpus the mutants were drawn from.

detected.description: Mutants the campaign ran and detected.

excluded.description: Mutants excluded because their identity leaked into the candidate snapshot; the exclusion is disclosed, never silent (RFC 0032, "Mutation challenge").

not_run.description: Mutants the campaign did not run. A non-zero count leaves the gate pending; it is never coverage.

undetected.description: Mutants the campaign ran and did not detect; each is named in `undetected_mutants`.

undetected_mutants.description: The specific mutants that were no longer detected (RFC 0032: the gate names the specific mutant).

vacuity_mutants.description: Non-vacuity mutants run within gate 6; availability collapse surfaces here (INV-012).

neighborhood_strategy.description: The eight closed plan §8.3 neighborhood strategies (RFC 0032, "Neighborhood construction"). The token is also the neighbor's class: a failing neighbor is disclosed with the strategy that generated it.

reuse_provenance.$comment: RFC 0032 F9, paid here. No field recorded the reuse-edge class, function_id, or function_version of a gate 5–7 result served from cache, so a reader could not distinguish a re-run campaign from a reused one, nor a Conservative reuse from a Validated one — leaving correction 1's distinction unauditable from a receipt.
reuse_provenance.description: Provenance of a gate 5–7 result served from the incremental cache rather than re-run (RFC 0032, "Cost governance"; RFC 0030). Absent means the campaign was re-run. The triple (class, function_id, function_version) is the quarantine unit: a quarantined triple drops to Experimental and cannot support promotion.

class.$comment: RFC 0030's closed reuse-edge class set has four members; `Experimental` is omitted here for the same reason `gates[].status` lists two of the five gate statuses. An Experimental edge MUST NOT support promotion, and by the meet rule one such edge anywhere in a derivation makes the whole derivation Experimental, so a gate resting on one cannot pass — and only passed gates reach a promotion receipt. Omitting the token makes an unpromotable reuse unrepresentable rather than merely prohibited by prose.
class.description: Reuse-edge class licensing this reuse (RFC 0030). A conservative disjointness judgement licenses `Conservative`; `Validated` requires a witness an independent checker accepts for this input digest, and MUST NOT be recorded for an over-approximation (RFC 0032 correction 1); an `Unknown` disjointness is dependent and re-runs, so it never appears here.

function_id.description: Registry name of the query definition the result was served under (RFC 0030).

function_version.description: Implementation version of that query definition (RFC 0030). It is not a release counter and MUST NOT be derived from the daemon version or from engine identity.

reused_units.description: How many neighborhood classes or mutants were served from cache rather than re-run.

redacted.$comment: mirrored from redacted.schema.json; identity-checked by the validator
redacted.description: Typed Redacted(reason, commitment) stub (plan §4.5). Mirrors redacted.schema.json; inlined to keep this file self-contained.

commitment.description: Content commitment (hash) of the redacted original.

original_class.description: Artifact class of the redacted original (plan §4.4 prefix, e.g. crash, ctx, proof).

allOf.description: RFC 0032 gate 5: a strategy truncated by budget leaves neighborhood pending with a continuation, so a receipt listing neighborhood passed cannot disclose a truncated strategy. Stated over the gate list rather than hardcoded, so the rule stays derived from what the receipt says it did.

description: The §8.2 gate-12 promotion receipt: every gate accounted for, before/after snapshots, the §8.6 cumulative cost ledger, unknowns, the policy decision, and the checker identity (INV-014) — the RFC 0032 receipt composition list.

base_snapshot.description: Before snapshot of the promoted transaction (RFC 0032 receipt composition).

toolchain.description: Toolchain identity of the checker build (INV-014).

cost_ledger.description: Cumulative cost ledger across all transaction versions (plan §8.6). Dimension keys mirror verification-task.schema.json's budget dimensions.

coverage.$comment: RFC 0032 F8, paid here. `coverage` was an untyped object with `additionalProperties: true`, so the per-strategy counts, the truncation disclosures, and — decisively — the failing-neighbor disclosure the ratified FR-05 counting rule depends on had no field to live in, and an adequacy measurement could not be graded mechanically against an unstructured blob. Each group is optional because a `not_yet_enforced` gate has no coverage to report; a gate listed `passed` whose group is absent is a disclosure failure this schema cannot yet detect (see the neighborhood conditional below for the case it can).
coverage.description: Coverage of the replay, neighborhood, mutation, refinement, certificate, and parity results (RFC 0032 receipt composition). Silent caps are prohibited: a truncated campaign is disclosed with its frontier and leaves its gate pending, and a receipt MUST NOT render coverage as adequacy — no adequacy claim exists until the docs/50-classified gaming corpus lands and is graded.

certificate_rebuild.description: Gate 9 coverage: invalidated certificates and proofs rebuilt with fresh checker identity and epochs (RFC 0032 gate table; RFC 0030's freshness predicate).

receipts.description: The rebuilt receipts this gate references.

stale.description: Artifacts still failing the freshness predicate. A non-zero count cannot support an Exact or Validated reuse edge.

defect_mutants.description: Gate 7 coverage: the known-defect mutant-corpus result set. An undetected defect mutant is instrumentation gaming.

incremental_parity.description: Gate 10 coverage: the Incremental Parity Audit promotion-lane comparison (RFC 0030). Sampling governs the interactive lane only, so a sampled comparison MUST NOT be presented here.

lane.$comment: The gate-10 rule is that only the promotion lane counts; the enum makes an interactive-lane comparison structurally distinguishable rather than indistinguishable.

mismatches.description: Comparisons that disagreed. A mismatch quarantines the implicated (class, function_id, function_version) triple.

neighborhood.description: Gate 5 coverage: per-strategy exploration counts plus every failing neighbor found. A single aggregate count is a rendering, not the record (RFC 0032 correction 13).

failing_neighbors.$comment: The ratified FR-05 counting rule (plan §24.5 quote-id=neighborhood-adequacy-catch-rate) counts a mutation as caught only when exploration surfaces a neighbor on which the patch fails AND the receipt discloses that neighbor. An undisclosed catch is not a catch, so this array is what the independent grader of research/33 grades; a run that finds a failing neighbor and omits it here has failed gate 5, not passed it. Post-promotion summarization MUST preserve this array.
failing_neighbors.description: Every neighbor on which the candidate fails, with its class and a handle to its run (RFC 0032, "Failing neighbors are disclosed").

neighbor.description: Identity of the failing neighbor within its strategy's enumeration.

run.description: Handle to the run that exhibited the failure, so the disclosure is auditable rather than asserted.

summary.description: Rendering only; never the sole home of a machine-consumable fact (INV-003).

strategies.description: One record per plan §8.3 strategy the campaign ran. A strategy the campaign did not run is omitted, and its absence is what distinguishes a broad campaign from one strategy run eight times.

allOf.description: Silent caps are prohibited (INV-007): a strategy truncated by budget discloses the committed frontier it was truncated at.

RFC 0032 F9: a strategy whose neighbors were served from cache discloses the reuse-edge class and the (function_id, function_version) it was served under, so a reused campaign is never rendered as a fresh one.

explored.description: Neighbors explored under this strategy, re-run and reused together.

failing.description: How many of the explored neighbors failed. It MUST equal the number of `failing_neighbors` entries carrying this strategy; the array, not this count, is the disclosure.

frontier.description: Committed frontier a truncated strategy stopped at, from which `repair.resume` continues monotonically.

reused.description: How many of the explored neighbors were served from the incremental cache rather than re-run.

truncated.description: Whether budget truncated this strategy. A truncated strategy leaves gate 5 pending with a continuation, never passed.

property_mutation.description: Gate 6 coverage: mutant-by-mutant detection results, including non-vacuity (RFC 0032 gate table).

refinement_coverage.description: Gate 8 coverage: the computed delta against the base (RFC 0032 correction 7). The gate passes iff coverage does not decrease, or the decrease is declared and permitted with the delta disclosed here; an uncomputable delta is inconclusive, never a passed gate.

declared_decrease.description: Whether a decrease was declared in the transaction and permitted by the evaluation policy. An undeclared decrease is a failed gate.

delta.description: after − before. A negative delta requires `declared_decrease` true.

replay.description: Gate 1 and gate 4 replay coverage: the base failure reproduced, and the exact failure no longer occurring on the candidate.

base_reproduced.description: Whether the original failure replayed on the base snapshot (gate 1). False is a failed gate; an engine divergence is inconclusive with a defect_* handle, not false.

candidate_clear.description: Whether the exact failure no longer occurs on the candidate under the original choices (gate 4).

runs.description: Replay runs this coverage is computed over.

epochs.description: Epoch pins for the receipt; mirrors proof-receipt.schema.json's epochs shape.

gate_profile.description: Phase-staged promotion profile (plan §21). Gates outside the profile are listed with status not_yet_enforced, never omitted.

gates.description: Gate identity, not count, is enforced: exactly twelve unique entries, one contains clause per §8.2 gate. Gate statuses use the canonical gate-status spelling shared with repair-transaction.schema.json; only passed and not_yet_enforced can appear on a promotion receipt.

intent_diff.$comment: RFC 0032 F7 stays open and is deferred, not paid: the agreement rule below is a relation between two sibling values, and JSON Schema draft 2020-12 has no comparison keyword — the same reason `semantic_epoch` and `epochs.semantic` cannot be forced to agree here. Collapsing the two fields into one would pay F7 properly but is a breaking change to a field RFC 0032's receipt-composition table names, so it belongs to an RFC 0032 revision rather than to a schema sweep. Until then the rule is stated here and checked by `evidence.verify`; the shipped example was corrected to satisfy it.
intent_diff.description: The intent diff. There is one diff artifact shape and the intent diff travels as the `intent_changes` set inside it (RFC 0031), so for a transaction with one classification this MUST name the same `diff_*` identity as `semantic_diff`. A receipt naming two different diff artifacts is malformed (RFC 0032 correction 10).

policy_decision.description: Promotion policy decision recorded in the receipt (RFC 0032 receipt composition); recomputed server-side at promotion time.

redacted_references.description: Redacted values referenced by this artifact (plan §4.5, §18.4).

result_snapshot.description: After snapshot the promotion produced (RFC 0032 receipt composition).

schema_id.description: Artifact-class identity of the governing schema: its `$id` with the `v<schema_epoch>/` segment removed (schemas/README.md). Stable across schema epochs.

schema_epoch.description: Schema epoch this instance was written against (schemas/README.md). It advances only on a breaking change to this artifact class, is not one of the six independently versioned epochs (RFC 0026 `rule versioning.epoch_independence`), and pins no semantics.

semantic_diff.description: The RFC 0031 classification this promotion was decided against. MUST name the same `diff_*` identity as `intent_diff` (RFC 0032 correction 10).

semantic_epoch.description: Semantic epoch the receipt is verifiable under. MUST agree with `epochs.semantic`; two spellings of one fact can disagree, and the schema cannot force their agreement (RFC 0032 F7).

unknowns.description: Unknowns carried into the promotion (RFC 0032 receipt composition).

title: Promotion Receipt
